From 6d05ff55ef4f4954d28551236239f297bd52ea48 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ngai-Mint Kwan <ngai-mint.kwan@intel.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Dec 2023 12:01:57 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] ice: Shut down VSI with "link-down-on-close" enabled

Disabling netdev with ethtool private flag "link-down-on-close" enabled
can cause NULL pointer dereference bug. Shut down VSI regardless of
"link-down-on-close" state.

Fixes: 8ac7132704f3 ("ice: Fix interface being down after reset with link-down-on-close flag on")
Reviewed-by: Przemek Kitszel <przemyslaw.kitszel@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Ngai-Mint Kwan <ngai-mint.kwan@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Wojciech Drewek <wojciech.drewek@intel.com>
Tested-by: Pucha Himasekhar Reddy <himasekharx.reddy.pucha@intel.com> (A Contingent worker at Intel)
Signed-off-by: Tony Nguyen <anthony.l.nguyen@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_main.c
index 270d68b69c59..adfdea1e2805 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_main.c
@@ -9193,6 +9193,8 @@ int ice_stop(struct net_device *netdev)
 			else
 				netdev_err(vsi->netdev, "Failed to set physical link down, VSI %d error %d\n",
 					   vsi->vsi_num, link_err);
+
+			ice_vsi_close(vsi);
 			return -EIO;
 		}
 	}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_main.c`**
   - A new line of code was added to the `ice_stop` function. Specifically, the line `ice_vsi_close(vsi);` was inserted after the error handling block that deals with setting the physical link down. This ensures that the Virtual Station Interface (VSI) is closed regardless of the state of the "link-down-on-close" flag.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a bug related to the handling of the "link-down-on-close" flag, which could lead to a NULL pointer dereference when disabling the network device. By ensuring that the VSI is closed in all cases, the patch prevents the potential crash that could occur if the device is disabled while the flag is enabled. This change is a direct response to the issue identified in the previous commit (8ac7132704f3), which aimed to fix the interface being down after a reset with the same flag. The new code enhances the robustness of the shutdown process for the VSI, thereby improving overall stability.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (test_bit(ICE_FLAG_LINK_DOWN_ON_CLOSE_ENA, vsi->back->flags)) {
    int link_err = ice_force_phys_link_state(vsi, false);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because when the "link-down-on-close" flag is enabled, the code attempts to change the physical link state without properly closing the VSI first. If the VSI is not closed correctly before the device is disabled, it can lead to a NULL pointer dereference when accessing uninitialized or invalid memory.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
ice_vsi_close(vsi);
```
Reason:
The fix ensures that the VSI is closed regardless of the state of the "link-down-on-close" flag. By calling `ice_vsi_close(vsi)` before returning an error or proceeding with the shutdown, it prevents the potential NULL pointer dereference by ensuring that the VSI is properly closed and resources are released before any further operations are attempted.
